broken: Mixed rendering across the cast (all stills): Tilly is a true cel with flat fills and a thick even outline. Sir Quill has a chrome helmet with environment reflections and soft orange-to-brown gradients on his legs (01a, 03, 09c). Vesper has an airbrushed teal head and glossy specular lips (05). Frost is a grainy brushed-metal toaster (01b, 08). Dash's hoodie is soft-shaded. Side by side they look like four asset packs, not one show. The outline is thick on Tilly and the toast, thin or missing on Quill's limbs and Vesper's body.

Dark limbs vanish against the navy set. Quill's maroon gloves and brown-maroon legs are close to background luma (01a, 01b, 03: the punching fist is a dark blob on navy). Vesper's dark legs merge with the chair shadow (01b, 07). Dash's navy legs disappear under his slump (06).

08 pick: Tilly's slump buries her head so far that she reads as a teal mop. The heart/drop/drop score pill sits right on top of her body, so the loser half of the joke cannot be read at 960x540. Only her feet poke out under the pill.
08: the 'The Ex' card overlaps Frost's name tag and cuts it to 'Frost' with the end clipped.

03 / 09c: the rival glare, which is the joke, is half off the right frame edge. Frost also has two slices with contradicting faces at once: the back slice glares and the front slice keeps its dot-eye smile. You cannot tell which face is Frost.
03 / 09b: Quill's 'victory punch' is a stiff level arm pointing off-left at shoulder height. It reads as a point or a salute, not a win. Nothing goes up, and the body does not lean or lift.

05: the 'bored, eyes rolled up' beat does not read. The visible eye looks forward and sideways, not up, and the mouth is wide open, so it reads as mid-speech or smug, not exhausted. There is no drawn half-lid.

07: the 'two-shot' has no shared eyeline. Vesper's head points at the camera, Tilly is seen from behind in three-quarter view walking past the chair, and the right half of the frame is empty lamp columns. Both characters are about 200 px tall, too small to carry a moment.
01a / 10c: Frost's walk-on legs dangle and splay like spider legs, and the waddle does not read as a waddle in a still. Tilly is half cut off by the left frame edge, with her face clipped.
06 / 10a: the survivors' poses are identical to the 01b wide, with no visible exhale or relief. In 06 Quill has turned so the back of his helmet faces the lens.
04: Tilly's face is cropped into the bottom-left corner under the caption box, a stray half-face crowding the cringe close-up.
Across stills, Frost's toast faces are inconsistent: heart eyes in 01a, dot-eye smile in 01b/06/08, an angry brow on a second slice in 03/09c.
slop: Purple gradient: Dash's hoodie is soft purple-to-violet gradient shading, not a two-step toon ramp (04 close-up, 02 left third, 01b, 06).
Gradient ball: Dash's pink head is a softly shaded sphere with an airbrushed falloff (04).
Default PBR look: Quill's chrome bucket helmet with environment-reflection specular streaks (03, 09a to 09c). This is the clearest 'imported 3D asset, default material' tell in the set.
Airbrushed gloss: Vesper's teal head and pink lips carry soft gradients and specular highlights, glossy vinyl rather than cel (05, 07).
Soft gradient shading on Quill's legs and cape, orange to brown (01a, 10c), and grainy brushed-metal shading on Frost's toaster body (01b, 08).
comprehension: Mostly yes for the format: the wides (01b, 06, 10a) read as a dating line-up, with a seated chooser on a riser and four contestants on lit spots. The phase reads from the round tag plus the dead lamp in 06. Who is winning is half clear: the cloud on Dash and the drop on Tilly read as losing, and the hearts on Quill and Frost read as winning, but nothing on the characters ranks Quill against Frost. Unclear: that Vesper is the star and the chooser (she is small and dim in the wide, and her close-up face carries no readable attitude); that anyone is betting; and in 08, who lost, because Tilly is an unreadable pile under a score pill. Most of the acting beats in shots.json (bored eye-roll, victory punch, rival glare, exhale) only read with the caption file beside them.
biggestGap: The reactions live in the emote icons, not on the characters. Next to tomodachi-03/04 and animalcrossing-01/03, where each face and silhouette carries the moment by itself, our non-human avatars barely change shape or face between beats. Next: give Frost, Quill and Vesper drawn swappable faces (toast brow and mouth, a squint or wide eye-slit for Quill, a half-lid texture for Vesper), and push every reaction pose about 2 to 3x until its silhouette alone tells the beat. Quill's fist goes above the helmet with the body leaning back, Tilly's slump keeps her head visible with the pill moved off her body, and Vesper's head tips back about 30 degrees.
protect: Tilly as a character: the 02/10b close-up (big glossy two-tone eyes, open mouth on a syllable, blush, thick even outline, mint and coral against navy) is the one shot that stands next to tomodachi-03 for charm. Keep her material, outline weight and face as the template the others are pulled toward.

The lit-spot wide (01b, 10a): each suitor stands in their own hard-edged beam on a colour-keyed ring with a matching name tag, and the four silhouettes (hoodie, chibi, bucket knight, toaster) stay distinct and countable at 960x540, the Take Me Out grammar done in toy form.

The drawn emote marks and Dash's cringe (04): the outlined heart and rain cloud sit over the head at about half head height, like the animalcrossing-02 '!', and Dash's visor eyes turn sad with a small frown under the cloud. That is a specific, readable moment. The dead-lamp slump in 06 also works, because Dash stays a readable dimmed silhouette rather than going black.
